question: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

On 22 May 2026, the European Chief Prosecutor sent a letter to the Commission1 with regard to an amendment to the Greek Code of Criminal Procedure, which introduces a special procedure for felonies committed by Members of the Greek Parliament, and the refusal of the Hellenic Supreme Judicial Council to recognise the full effect of the decision taken by the College of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) to renew the mandate of three European Delegated Prosecutors for five years. The letter also refers to a negative effect on the EPPO’s ability to effectively investigate and prosecute offences under its competence, a negative effect on the EPPO’s independence in Greece and serious doubts as to the Greek authorities’ compliance with their obligation of sincere cooperation under Article 4(3) TEU. The fact that the letter was sent in accordance with recital 16 of Regulation (EU) 2020/2092 on a general regime of conditionality for the protection of the Union budget2 raises concerns as to the potential triggering of the procedures set out in the Regulation. In the interest of preventing any loss of funds, can the Commission say: 1.
Has it examined the letter from the European Chief Prosecutor?
How does it assess the recent legislative amendments and decisions in Greece referred to in the letter?
What measures does it intend to propose to the Greek Government in order to address the serious concerns raised by the European Chief Prosecutor in her letter?

https://www.eppo.europa.eu/en/media/news/statement-regarding-recent-developments-affectingeffective-and-independent-functioning. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32020R2092. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.7.2026) The Commission attaches great attention to the concerns and issues brought to its attention by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO), in particular where the EPPO considers that they may affect its ability to effectively carry out the tasks entrusted to it under the EPPO Regulation1. In the present case, the Commission has monitored the developments closely and is currently assessing all the information available and received, as well as the concerns raised by the EPPO. The Commission will also continue to follow any further developments.
1 Council Regulation (EU) 2017/1939 of 12 October 2017 implementing enhanced cooperation on the
establishment of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO), OJ L 283, 31.10.2017, p. 1.
